title: Zero-pad percent-encoding for code points below 0x10 in UriTemplate
body:
## Problem

`pctEncode` in `src/vs/base/common/uriTemplate.ts` builds escapes without zero-padding:

```ts
out += '%' + chr.toString(16).toUpperCase();
```

For any code point `< 0x10`, `toString(16)` yields a **single** hex digit, so the function emits a one-digit escape instead of the RFC 3986 / RFC 6570 mandated two-digit form:

| input char | code | before | expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| tab | 0x09 | `%9` | `%09` |
| newline | 0x0A | `%A` | `%0A` |
| carriage return | 0x0D | `%D` | `%0D` |
| bell | 0x07 | `%7` | `%07` |

The result is a malformed URI; `decodeURIComponent` rejects it with `URI malformed`. `UriTemplate` resolves MCP and agent resource URIs (e.g. `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/`, `src/vs/platform/agentHost/`), so a variable value containing a control character produces a broken URL.

## Reproduction

Running the real `UriTemplate` (transpiled):

```
UriTemplate.parse('{x}').resolve({ x: 'a\tb' })  ->  'a%9b'   (expected 'a%09b')
decodeURIComponent('a%9b')                        ->  throws URI malformed
```

## Fix

Zero-pad to two hex digits:

```ts
out += '%' + chr.toString(16).toUpperCase().padStart(2, '0');
```

`padStart` is a no-op for code points `>= 0x10`, so existing escapes (`%20`, `%21`, `%3B`, …) are unchanged — verified against the existing test expectations.

## Test

Adds a regression test in `src/vs/base/test/common/uriTemplate.test.ts` asserting `{x}` with `'a\tb'`, `'\n'`, `'\r'` resolve to `a%09b`, `%0A`, `%0D`.

title: chat: restore last-used agent and model for new chat editors
body:
- New chat editors always opened with the Local agent and the Auto model, even right after the user had been working with an agent host (e.g. Copilot Agent Host). The last-used agent/model was never consulted, so users had to re-pick the agent, model, and model configuration for every new editor, and it reset in every new workspace.
- Persists the last-used non-local chat agent (session type) at profile scope and prefers it when resolving the session type for a new chat editor, so the editor reopens with the agent the user last worked with across windows and workspaces. An explicit `chat.editor.defaultProvider` still wins.
- Restores that agent's last-used model and its configuration (e.g. context size, thinking effort) for the fresh editor session, mirroring the existing reopened-session restore.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322792

title: smoke: retry Electron launch to survive intermittent fontconfig startup crash
body:
## The expat upgrade did not work — here's why, and the fix that will

PR #323001 installed libexpat 2.8.1 and **it still crashed** ([run 28192795744](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/28192795744/job/83511550358)). I pulled the new crash dumps and walked the frame-pointer (RBP) stack:

```
#0  libc.so.6 +0x48806          (NULL deref — identical in every dump)
#1  libexpat.so.1 +0x1d9f3      (2.8.1 — offsets CHANGED, so the new lib IS loaded)
#2  libexpat.so.1 +0xa107
#3-8 libfontconfig.so.1 +0x2f6c9 / +0x3022d / +0x30479 / +0x173cd / +0x121c1 / +0x176bd   (IDENTICAL to the 2.6.1 dumps)
#9  libpangoft2-1.0.so.0 +0xc225
#10 libglib-2.0.so.0 +0x8be62   (glib worker thread)
```

The expat offsets moved (proving 2.8.1 was actually loaded in the crashing process), but the crash is unchanged. **expat is exonerated.** The constant factors are **libfontconfig + libc + the pango worker-thread init** (`pango init_in_thread → FcInit`). fontconfig hands expat a bad/NULL pointer (or a race corrupts it) and *any* expat version faithfully derefs it. This is a **nondeterministic startup race in the system font stack**, not an application bug and not fixable by swapping expat. (It also explains the earlier "less XML made it worse" result — timing, not content.)

## Fix: retry the launch

The crash happens **at launch, before any window**, and is rare *per launch* (~0.8%). But a smoke run does ~25 launches, so it compounds into the ~8–19% *per-run* failure we've been seeing. Retrying the launch collapses that to near-zero with effectively zero overhead on the normal path (retries almost never trigger).

- `Application#start()`: retry launch + window-ready up to 3×, tearing down the crashed instance between attempts.
- `playwrightElectron`: close the Electron app if it produced no window, so a retried launch doesn't leak a stray process.
- smoke `installAppBeforeHandler`: widen the before-hook timeout to accommodate retries.

This pairs with the already-merged fail-fast launch error (#322905): a crashed launch now fails in ~60s instead of hanging to the 120s hook timeout, which is what makes the retries affordable.

## Why retry instead of "fix the crash"

The fault is in **system libraries** (fontconfig/pango/glib) during Electron startup on the CI image — an environment/infra flake, not VS Code code. Retrying a known-infra-flaky startup is standard practice and idiomatic here (the harness already retries the Electron download, app exit, etc.). The underlying fontconfig/pango race can be chased separately (e.g. a newer libfontconfig), but retry makes CI green regardless of root cause.

## Supersedes / related
- #322905 (merged) — fail-fast on launch crash.
- #322994 — revert of the DOCTYPE change that regressed crash rate (keep).
- #323001 — expat 2.8.1 install: **does not fix the crash**, recommend closing.

title: ci: install CVE-fixed libexpat to fix fontconfig SIGSEGV in Electron smoke tests
body:
Supersedes the from-source build idea — installs a prebuilt official Ubuntu `.deb`, fetched from the **Azure Ubuntu mirror the runner already uses**. Also includes the revert of #322909 (so it works whether or not the standalone revert #322994 lands first).

## Root cause (confirmed)

Intermittent Linux `Electron-Smoke` failures are a **SIGSEGV in `libexpat` during fontconfig parsing at Electron startup**, before any window appears. Frame-pointer (RBP) backtrace from a CI crash dump (run 28188049700):

```
#0  libc.so.6        (NULL deref, fault addr 0x0)
#1-3 libexpat.so.1   (XML_ParseBuffer ...)
#4-9 libfontconfig.so.1  (FcInit / config parse)
#10 libpangoft2-1.0.so.0
#11 libglib-2.0.so.0  (worker thread)
#12 libc.so.6        (thread start)
```

Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) ships **libexpat1 2.6.1**; the relevant parser NULL-deref fixes are only in **expat ≥ 2.7.5**, which noble hasn't packaged. Earlier fontconfig-config tweaks only perturbed timing (removing the `<!DOCTYPE>` in #322909 actually *doubled* the crash rate, ~8% → ~19% — reverted here).

## Fix

Install the official prebuilt **`libexpat1` 2.8.1 `.deb`** onto the noble runner:

- Fetched from the **Azure Ubuntu mirror the runner already uses** (`azure.archive.ubuntu.com`, in-datacenter), falling back to the canonical Ubuntu archive and then Launchpad's permanent store. All three serve the **byte-identical** official build; we **pin the sha256**.
- That package `Pre-Depends: libc6 (>= 2.38)` only, and noble has libc6 **2.39**, so `dpkg -i` installs it cleanly with no dependency conflict.
- It replaces the system `libexpat.so.1` (ABI-stable SONAME) for **every** process, including the Electron browser process where the crash happens — no `LD_PRELOAD` needed.
- The step **auto-skips** once the runner ships `libexpat1 >= 2.7.5` (so it self-removes when noble backports the fix).

The minimal fontconfig config (DOCTYPE restored via the revert) is kept as secondary stabilization.

## Why not plain `apt install libexpat1` / why this source

- noble's apt pocket only carries **2.6.1**; the fix lives in newer releases (questing 2.7.1, resolute 2.7.4, stonking 2.8.1).
- `packages.microsoft.com` and `dl.google.com` (the runner's other apt origins) don't carry `libexpat1`.
- The Azure mirror is a full mirror of the Ubuntu archive, so its **pool** hosts the newer-release deb too — byte-identical to Launchpad (verified). So this *is* "use the package manager's source", just pulling a build noble's own pocket doesn't carry yet.

## Validation

- Workflow YAML parses; no duplicate steps.
- Verified the 2.8.1 deb `Pre-Depends: libc6 (>= 2.38)` (installs on noble's 2.39).
- Verified the Azure mirror, the Ubuntu archive, and Launchpad all return the deb with the **same sha256**; simulated the download+verify loop end-to-end.
- Real proof is CI crash-rate; companion PR #322905 (fail-fast launch) surfaces any residual crash quickly instead of as a 120s opaque timeout.

title: Revert "ci: drop external DTD from minimal fontconfig to avoid expat NULL-deref crash (#322909)"
body:
Reverts the fontconfig change from #322909.

## Why revert

The change was intended to reduce the intermittent fontconfig/expat SIGSEGV that crashes Electron at smoke-test launch. **It did the opposite.**

Measured on the `pr.yml` workflow (the `Linux / Electron-Smoke` job specifically), around the merge of #322909 (2026-06-25 13:06 UTC):

| | smoke failures / completed | rate |
|---|---|---|
| **Before** merge | 1 / 13 | ~8% |
| **After** merge | 8 / 43 | ~19% |

The failure rate roughly doubled.

## What the dump actually shows

I pulled a crash dump from an after-merge failure (run 28188049700, `Language Features` suite) and walked the **frame-pointer (RBP) chain** — more reliable than the heuristic stack scan used to justify #322909:

```
#0  libc.so.6           (NULL deref, fault addr 0x0)
#1  libexpat.so.1
#2  libexpat.so.1
#3  libexpat.so.1
#4  libfontconfig.so.1
#5  libfontconfig.so.1
#6  libfontconfig.so.1
#7  libfontconfig.so.1
#8  libfontconfig.so.1
#9  libfontconfig.so.1
#10 libpangoft2-1.0.so.0
#11 libglib-2.0.so.0
#12 libc.so.6
```

It's the **same** `pango → fontconfig → expat → libc` NULL-deref as before, just more frequent. The original "external parameter entity via DOCTYPE" theory doesn't hold: the minimal config without the DOCTYPE parses *less* XML than the system config, yet crashes *more*. That points at a flaky race / heap issue in the expat 2.6.1 + fontconfig stack that removing the DOCTYPE perturbed, not a deterministic content bug.

## Net

Restore the previous (lower) crash rate now. The durable fix is still getting `libexpat >= 2.7.5` onto the runner — the workaround step already auto-disables itself when it detects that version. That will be pursued separately.

Companion harness PR #322905 (fail fast on launch crash) stays in; it doesn't affect crash frequency, only how quickly/clearly a crash is surfaced.

title: Agent Host client tool hangs after active client removal; browser click invoked with empty args

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue identified by VS Code Team member as probable bug

labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
## Summary

A browser `clickElement` tool call can get stuck in `Preparing` after the Agent Host removes the active client. The click never reaches Playwright; the workbench invokes the browser tool with `{}` parameters and crashes during tool preparation.

## Observed

In an Agents/Copilot CLI session using built-in browser tools:

1. `openBrowserPage` succeeds.
2. `clickElement` on the initial `Start` button succeeds.
3. `screenshotPage` succeeds.
4. The next `clickElement` on the board's `Run` button stays stuck at `Preparing`.

The session event stream ends with:

```text
tool.execution_start clickElement
permission.requested clickElement
# no permission.completed
# no tool.execution_complete
```

## Key log evidence

The model requested valid arguments:

```json
{
  "element": "Run button on Research Agent",
  "pageId": "<page-id>",
  "ref": "e200"
}
```

But the workbench invoked the underlying browser tool with empty parameters:

```text
[AgentHost] Invoking client tool: clickElement
[LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool] Invoking tool click_element with parameters {}
[error] Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')
    at createBrowserPageLink(...)
    at ClickBrowserTool.prepareToolInvocation(...)
```

The AHP sequence for the same tool call was:

```text
chat/toolCallStart clickElement
chat/toolCallReady confirmed="not-needed"           # no toolInput
chat/toolCallComplete success=false error="Client <client-id> disconnected before completing clickElement"
chat/toolCallReady confirmation UI with real toolInput
```

About 6 seconds earlier, the same session received:

```text
session/activeClientRemoved clientId=<client-id>
```

## Suspected cause

This looks like an Agent Host/client-tool lifecycle race:

- The active client is removed from session state while the UI/client connection is still participating in the turn.
- A later client-contributed browser tool call is treated as orphaned/disconnected.
- The synthetic `toolCallReady` without `toolInput` is consumed by the workbench client-tool handler.
- The handler falls back to `{}` and invokes `click_element` before the later `toolCallReady` containing the real `toolInput` arrives.
- `ClickBrowserTool.prepareToolInvocation` assumes `pageId` is present, calls `createBrowserPageLink(undefined)`, throws, and the original Copilot tool execution remains stuck waiting for completion/permission state.

Relevant code paths:

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts`
  - disconnected client tool call handling emits synthetic ready/complete events
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts`
  - missing `toolInput` falls back to `{}` once status is not `Streaming`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/tools/clickBrowserTool.ts`
  - `prepareToolInvocation` assumes `pageId` is defined

## Expected

A disconnected/orphaned client-tool call should fail cleanly and unblock the model/UI, or be retried with a replacement active client. It should not invoke the local browser tool with `{}` parameters or leave the tool call stuck in `Preparing`.

## Possible fixes

- Do not invoke client tools from `toolCallReady` events that lack `toolInput` when the tool has required arguments or `_meta.toolArguments` exists.
- Ensure disconnected-client synthetic `toolCallReady`/`toolCallComplete` ordering cannot race with later confirmation UI events for the same tool call.
- Harden browser tool `prepareToolInvocation` against missing `pageId` so malformed protocol state becomes a clean tool error.
- Investigate why `session/activeClientRemoved` fired while the client was still successfully confirming/completing tool calls in the same session.

title: Feature Request: Support Third-Party API Configuration in GitHub Copilot
body:
# Feature Request: Support Third-Party API Configuration in GitHub Copilot

## Summary

I propose that GitHub Copilot in VSCode should support user-configurable third-party API endpoints, allowing developers to use alternative language models (e.g., Mimo, DeepSeek, Ollama local models) alongside the official Copilot models.

---

## Problem Statement

Currently, GitHub Copilot only supports models provided by GitHub/OpenAI. Users cannot configure their own API endpoints, which creates several limitations:

| Limitation | Impact |
|------------|--------|
| **Restricted Model Choice** | Users cannot use other high-quality models (e.g., Mimo V2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V4, local Ollama models) |
| **Cost Opacity** | Users cannot choose more cost-effective API providers |
| **Privacy Concerns** | Sensitive code must be sent to GitHub servers |
| **Network Restrictions** | Some regions cannot directly access GitHub API |
| **No BYOK Option** | Users with existing API keys from other providers cannot utilize them |

---

## Proposed Solution

### Option A: Settings Configuration (Recommended)

Add a new configuration option in VSCode settings:

```json
{
  "github.copilot.customModels": [
    {
      "id": "mimo-v2.5-pro",
      "name": "Mimo V2.5 Pro",
      "vendor": "mimo",
      "baseUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1",
      "apiKey": "${env:MY_API_KEY}",
      "model": "mimo-v2.5-pro",
      "capabilities": {
        "chat": true,
        "completions": true,
        "maxTokens": 8192,
        "maxInputTokens": 200000
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### Option B: Enhanced Language Model API

Leverage and extend the existing proposed API (`vscode.lm`):

```typescript
// Allow extensions to register custom model providers
vscode.lm.registerLanguageModelChatProvider('custom-provider', {
  provideLanguageModelChat() {
    return {
      id: 'custom-model',
      name: 'Custom Model',
      vendor: 'custom',
      // ... model configuration
    };
  }
});
```

### Option C: Hybrid Mode

- Retain official Copilot models
- Add support for user-configured third-party APIs
- Allow switching via UI dropdown

---

## Use Cases

1. **Enterprise Users**: Companies with private LLM deployments need to route Copilot requests through their own infrastructure
2. **Cost Optimization**: Users can choose cheaper API providers for non-critical tasks
3. **Privacy Compliance**: Sensitive code stays within company networks
4. **Regional Accessibility**: Users in restricted regions can use alternative API endpoints
5. **Model Diversity**: Developers can leverage specialized models for specific tasks

---

## Technical Feasibility

VSCode already has the foundational APIs:

| API | Status | Description |
|-----|--------|-------------|
| `vscode.lm.selectChatModels()` | Proposed | Select available language models |
| `vscode.lm.sendRequest()` | Proposed | Send requests to language models |
| `languageModelChatProviders` | Proposed | Extensions can register model providers |

The **Mimo for Copilot** extension already demonstrates this is possible using the proposed API. The infrastructure exists; it just needs official support in the Copilot extension.

---

## Expected Benefits

| Benefit | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Increased User Satisfaction** | Users can freely choose their preferred models |
| **Ecosystem Growth** | Attracts more API providers to integrate |
| **Competitive Advantage** | Matches features of Cursor, Windsurf, and other AI-powered editors |
| **Community Contribution** | Developers can contribute extensions and tools |
| **Enterprise Adoption** | Enterprises can deploy Copilot with their private models |

---

## Existing Implementations

Several third-party extensions have successfully implemented this pattern:

| Extension | Approach |
|-----------|----------|
| **Mimo for Copilot** | Uses proposed `languageModelChatProviders` API |
| **Continue.dev** | Standalone extension with multi-API support |
| **Cline / Roo Code** | Standalone extension with OpenAI-compatible API support |

This demonstrates both the demand and technical feasibility.

---

## Comparison with Competitors

| Editor | Third-Party API Support |
|--------|------------------------|
| **VSCode + Copilot** | ❌ Not supported |
| **Cursor** | ✅ Supports custom models |
| **Windsurf** | ✅ Supports custom models |
| **Zed** | ✅ Supports custom models |

Adding this feature would bring VSCode to parity with competing editors.

---

## Conclusion

Supporting third-party API configuration in GitHub Copilot would:

1. ✅ Enhance user experience and choice
2. ✅ Strengthen VSCode's competitive position
3. ✅ Foster ecosystem development
4. ✅ Meet community demand
5. ✅ Enable enterprise adoption

This is a win-win proposal that benefits users, developers, and the VSCode ecosystem.

---

## Additional Context

- VSCode is open-source (MIT License)
- GitHub Copilot is a closed-source extension
- The community has been requesting this feature
- Technical infrastructure already exists via proposed APIs

---

**Thank you for considering this proposal.**

---

It would be highly beneficial to introduce an opt-in "Listen to PRs" background feature that monitors active Pull Requests for incoming review comments and integrates directly with Copilot Chat to streamline the feedback loop.

Currently, context switching between PR review platforms and the IDE to address comments is a manual and disruptive process. This feature would automatically capture PR feedback and present actionable, AI-driven resolution paths directly within VS Code.

**Proposed Implementation:**

*   **Smart Notification System:** Upon receiving PR comments, VS Code triggers a toast notification. This system should include a configurable debounce/delay (e.g., 2-3 minutes) to batch multiple comments into a single notification and account for immediate reviewer retractions.
*   **Triage Actions:** The consolidated notification should offer three primary resolution paths:
    1.  **Review Manually:** Opens the standard PR diff view for human intervention.
    2.  **Suggest with Copilot:** Opens a new Copilot Chat session, automatically attaching the relevant file context and pre-filling a prompt based on the reviewer's feedback. The user can then review, edit, and send the prompt.
    3.  **Auto (Agentic Mode):** Delegates the resolution to Copilot, allowing it to autonomously perform code changes to address the feedback or draft direct replies to the PR comments.
*   **Context Menu Enhancement:** Extend the existing `+` (Add Context) menu in the Copilot Chat UI to explicitly include "PR Comments" as a selectable data source, enabling users to easily bind review feedback to standard chat queries.

This workflow significantly reduces the friction of the code review process, allowing developers to leverage AI to resolve PR feedback seamlessly and efficiently.

title: [Feature] Enable/Disable Extensions from the .vscode Folder
body:
### Description

I've been using VS Code for a long time, primarily for web application development, and have accumulated a large number of installed extensions over time.

I'd like to propose a feature that allows enabling and disabling extensions per project via the `.vscode` folder, using either an `extensions.json` or `settings.json` file. Specifically, it would be great to define arrays to toggle extensions on or off for the current workspace.

#### Example:

```json
{
  "extensions_enabled": [
    "esbenp.prettier-vscode",
    "dbaeumer.vscode-eslint",
    "bradlc.vscode-tailwindcss"
  ],
  "extensions_disabled": [
    "ms-vscode.vscode-typescript-next"
  ]
}
```

### Justification

While VS Code supports profiles that allow managing extension sets globally, many projects don't require all installed extensions to be active. For example, a NestJS project typically doesn't need HTML, CSS, or JavaScript syntax styling extensions — yet they may still be loaded, consuming valuable system memory.

This feature would:
- Reduce RAM usage per project.
- Improve performance by loading only relevant extensions.
- Provide a more focused and lightweight development experience.
- Allow teams to standardize extension usage across a project.

### Additional Context

This would be similar to how workspace settings already override user settings, but specifically for extension lifecycle management.

Would love to hear feedback from the team and community on this idea.

title: fix: guard WorkspaceTrustEditor.render against disposed instantiation service (fixes #322973)
body:
### Summary

`unhandlederror-InstantiationService has been disposed` (369 hits / 336 users, all in `1.126.0`) is a **use-after-dispose race** in the Workspace Trust editor. `WorkspaceTrustEditor.render()` is decorated with `@debounce(100)`, which schedules the actual render via `setTimeout(..., 100)`. The `@debounce` decorator stores the timer on the instance but never cancels it on dispose. When the user closes the editor group within that 100 ms window, the group view's **scoped `InstantiationService`** (the same service injected into the pane) is disposed together with the pane. The leaked debounce timer then fires and calls `this.instantiationService.createInstance(Link, ...)` on the now-disposed service, which throws from `_throwIfDisposed()`.

The fix adds an early-return guard at the top of the debounced `render()` so the stale callback does nothing once the pane (and its scoped service) has been disposed.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#322973
Recommended reviewer: `@rwoll`

### Culprit Commit

Not attributable to a single regression commit.

- The crashing pattern is **structural and pre-existing**: `@debounce(100)` on `render()` combined with the editor pane's scoped `InstantiationService` being disposed on group teardown. The `@debounce` decorator (`src/vs/base/common/decorators.ts`) has never cancelled its `setTimeout` on dispose.
- `git blame` is unavailable in this environment — CI uses a shallow/grafted clone (only the shipped commit `7e7950df89d055b5a378379db9ee14290772148a` is present), so every line attributes to the graft.
- The most recent change to `workspaceTrustEditor.ts` is PR #322130 (`1c28070e`, `@rwoll`, 2026-06-19), but it only **removed the "Trust Parent" button** (+1/−20) and does not touch the debounce, the disposal path, or the crashing header-link render block — so it is not the root cause.
- The bucket is reported only in `1.126.0` (first seen 2026-06-24). The `recent-regression` signal most likely reflects an editor lifecycle/timing shift elsewhere or telemetry retention rather than a code change to this file; the latent race itself is old.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Evt as Trust / settings event
    participant WTE as WorkspaceTrustEditor
    participant Timer as setTimeout (`@debounce`)
    participant Grp as EditorGroupView
    participant ISvc as scoped InstantiationService

    Evt->>WTE: onDidChangeTrust → render()
    WTE->>Timer: `@debounce`(100) schedules setTimeout
    Note over Grp,ISvc: User closes the editor group (< 100 ms)
    Grp->>ISvc: dispose() (registered via _register)
    Grp->>WTE: dispose() (pane + its _store)
    Timer-->>WTE: timer fires → render() body runs
    WTE->>ISvc: createInstance(Link, ...) at line 873
    ISvc-->>WTE: throw "InstantiationService has been disposed"
```

### Affected Files

- **`src/vs/workbench/contrib/workspace/browser/workspaceTrustEditor.ts`** (fixed) — `render()` is `@debounce(100)` (line 843); crash site is `this.instantiationService.createInstance(Link, ...)` at line 873 (and the same call reached via `renderAffectedFeatures` → `renderLimitationsListElement`, line 1106). The injected `@IInstantiationService` is the editor group's scoped service.
- `src/vs/base/common/decorators.ts` (evidence) — `@debounce` schedules `setTimeout(() => fn.apply(this, args), delay)` and never clears it on dispose (frame `decorators.ts:83`).
- `src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiationService.ts` (evidence) — `_throwIfDisposed()` throws `InstantiationService has been disposed`; called by `createInstance` (line 119).
- `src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorGroupView.ts` (evidence) — line 201 `this.scopedInstantiationService = this._register(this.instantiationService.createChild(...))` proves the pane's injected service is disposed when the group is torn down.

### Repro Steps

1. Open a folder in **Restricted Mode** (untrusted).
2. Open the Workspace Trust editor (command **Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust**).
3. Cause a state change that the editor listens to (toggle trust, or change a restricted setting / trusted folder) so `render()` gets debounced.
4. Within ~100 ms, close the editor (or close/replace its editor group) so the pane and its scoped `InstantiationService` are disposed.
5. The leaked debounce timer fires after disposal and calls `createInstance` on the disposed service → `InstantiationService has been disposed` is thrown and reported to telemetry.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/workspace/browser/workspaceTrustEditor.ts`:

Add a guard as the first statement of the debounced `render()`:

```ts
if (this._store.isDisposed) {
    return;
}
```

This applies the use-after-dispose remedy at the place where the deferred work runs: once the owning object has been disposed, its leaked timer callback must do nothing. It is **not** a crash-site guard masking another component — the object that schedules the debounced callback (`WorkspaceTrustEditor`) is the very object that gets disposed, so checking its own `_store.isDisposed` is the correct producer-side lifecycle check. `this._store` is the `protected` `DisposableStore` every `Disposable` owns, and the pane plus its scoped `InstantiationService` are disposed together on group teardown, so `this._store.isDisposed` is a reliable signal that the injected service is gone. Because `render()` runs fully synchronously (no `await` between entry and the `createInstance` calls), this single top-of-method guard covers both the reported crash at line 873 and the sibling `createInstance` reached via `renderAffectedFeatures` → `renderLimitationsListElement` (line 1106). This matches an idiomatic VS Code pattern used widely across the workbench (terminal, chat, mcp, notebook, extensions) for guarding deferred work after self-disposal.

After this change, the debounced `render()` cannot reach `this.instantiationService.createInstance(...)` after the pane is disposed, because the new first-line guard returns early whenever `this._store.isDisposed` is `true` — which is always the case once the group view's disposal has torn down both the pane and its scoped `InstantiationService`.

**Alternatives considered:**

- *Make the debounce cancellable* (replace `@debounce` with a `RunOnceScheduler` registered via `this._register` and cancelled on dispose) — rejected as a larger, riskier change to a shared decorator / working method when a minimal, idiomatic guard fully prevents the race.
- *Wrap the `createInstance` call in `try/catch`* — rejected because it would hide the error from the telemetry pipeline instead of preventing the use-after-dispose, violating the do-not-silence-errors principle.
- *Guard at the crash site (line 873)* — rejected because that is the symptom location; the correct fix prevents the entire stale render pass from running, not just one of its `createInstance` calls.

### Recommended Owner

**`@rwoll`** (Ross Wollman) — the most recent active owner of `workspaceTrustEditor.ts` (PR #322130, 2026-06-19, days before the regression window), so best positioned to review a lifecycle fix in this editor. title: fix(oss): make cached-NOTICE fallback download match files
body:
🤖 AI Assisted PR

## What

The cached-NOTICE fallback in the Quality stage never actually downloaded the cached NOTICE, because both `DownloadBuildArtifacts@1` steps used a brace-expansion `itemPattern`:

```yaml
itemPattern: "**/{ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt,notice-meta.txt}"
```

`DownloadBuildArtifacts@1` runs minimatch with brace expansion **disabled**, so this pattern matches **zero** files. The `notice_output` artifact downloads, but every file is filtered out before it hits disk — and the downstream "apply NOTICE fallback" step then correctly reports "No cached NOTICE available".

## How it surfaced

Build **450982** is the first real Component Governance (`notice@0`) outage on `main` since the cutover. The fallback chain fired exactly as designed, but the same-branch download logged:

```
Pattern: **/{ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt,notice-meta.txt}
0 matches
0 final results
Item excluded: notice_output/ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt   ← the file was right there
```

So the build proceeded without a cached CG NOTICE even though a perfectly good one existed on the branch's previous build.

The bug has been latent since the original CG PR (#322410) — these download steps only run on a genuine CG failure, and every validation build so far had CG succeed (steps skipped), so it was never exercised until now.

## The fix

Replace the brace pattern with one plain glob per line in **both** download steps (same-branch + main-fallback):

```yaml
itemPattern: |
  **/ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt
  **/notice-meta.txt
```

Plain globs are matched reliably by `DownloadBuildArtifacts@1`. The hardcoded download paths were already correct — only the file filter was broken.

## Validation

- Reproduced the brace-vs-plain matching difference against the exact artifact file list from build 450982.
- The build log confirms the artifact downloaded and the named file was present but excluded — so a working filter lands it at the path the apply step already expects.
- No code path changes; this only widens what the fallback download retrieves.

title: sessions: save unstarted session drafts on navigation and exit
body:
# Propose Draft State Preservation for Unstarted Session Composers

Proposes configuring a conditional `draftStorageKey` on `NewChatInputWidget` to persist the unsent draft state of unstarted session composers when navigating away from them (e.g. into active sessions) and upon application exit.

### Problem
Previously, when the user opened the "New Session" compose view in the Agents Window, typed a draft, and navigated to a previous session in the sidebar/history, the unstarted `NewChatView` was disposed without saving. Because there was no disposal save trigger, any typed draft was immediately lost. 

Additionally, both the main unstarted session composer and any in-session sub-chats (`NewChatInSessionWidget`) instantiated `NewChatInputWidget` and shared the same global storage key (`'sessions.draftState'`), which would lead to collisions.

### Solution
1. **Disposal-Safe Saving**: `NewChatInputWidget` now invokes its `saveState()` method during `dispose()`. This ensures that navigating away from an unstarted session safely commits the current draft text and attachments.
2. **Key Isolation**: Added a `draftStorageKey` property to the input widget options. 
   - `NewChatWidget` (the home screen compose view) passes `'sessions.draftState'` as its storage key, enabling saving and restoring.
   - `NewChatInSessionWidget` (the in-session sub-chats) leaves it undefined, ensuring they never read or write to the global composer draft key and eliminating draft collisions.

### Goal of this Draft PR
This PR is opened as a draft/reference implementation to demonstrate the clarified draft state management. The goal is to:
- Propose this lightweight fix to the draft state management lifecycle.
- Obtain feedback and early validation from the team regarding the approach.
- Seek guidance if a different architecture or a dedicated draft service is preferred for managing persistent unstarted drafts.

Closes #315996

title: sessions: surface un-accepted PR review comments to the agent
body:
Fixes #322172

## Problem  When working with agent feedback in an agent-host session, un-accepted **PR review comments** were invisible to the agent. The agent-host `listComments` tool appends a note ("there are N pull request comments which the user has not reviewed yet") and the `viewUnreviewedComments` tool reveals those comments — but both read **only** agent-feedback annotations whose `_meta` is `kind: 'prReview'` + `state: 'created'`.  Un-accepted PR review comments lived only client-side in `CodeReviewService` (`prReviewState`, keyed by session resource) and were never written to the session's annotations channel. So the note always said zero and `viewUnreviewedComments` returned nothing. (The channel-key resolution itself is fine: the server already normalizes peer-chat URIs to the owning session, and the client resolves the channel via `session.sessionId`, so a session's comments stay on one channel across multiple chats.)  ## Fix  Add `AgentFeedbackPRReviewSeederContribution`, which mirrors the active agent-host session's un-accepted PR review comments onto the feedback annotations channel as `created` `prReview` items, **keyed by the session resource** (the same key every other feedback op uses). Each mirror carries `sourcePRReviewCommentId` so it can be de-duplicated against the raw PR comment in the editor and so resolving it resolves the originating GitHub thread.  The seeder is idempotent and self-healing: - seeds a `created` mirror for each PR comment that has none; - refreshes a `created` mirror's text when the upstream comment body changes; - collapses duplicate `created` mirrors for the same source (benign echo race / two windows); - removes a `created` mirror when its source PR comment disappears (resolved upstream, converted, or dismissed), while keeping accepted/submitted mirrors.  Supporting changes: - `IAgentFeedbackItemsBackend.hasLoaded` / `IAgentFeedbackService.hasLoadedFeedback` (+ a one-time "snapshot loaded" event) so the seeder waits for the authoritative annotations snapshot before acting — avoiding duplicate mirrors on reload. - `ICodeReviewService.dismissPRReviewComment`: deleting a comment from the `viewUnreviewedComments` confirmation now suppresses the source PR comment so the seeder does not immediately recreate the mirror. - `getSessionEditorComments` de-duplicates the two representations in the editor: a still-`created` mirror is hidden (raw PR comment shown with its native actions); once accepted/submitted the mirror supersedes the raw comment.  ## Notes for reviewers  - Only the **active** session is seeded by design — `CodeReviewService` only loads PR review threads for the active session, and mirrors persist as server-side annotations so they survive a session going inactive. This is documented in the seeder. - A rubber-duck review was run; findings (stale mirror content, non-sticky delete, active-session rationale) were addressed, plus a self-healing duplicate-collapse for the snapshot-echo race. - Tests added: seeder behavior (`agentFeedbackPRReviewSeeder.test.ts`), editor de-dup (`sessionEditorComments.test.ts`), and `dismissPRReviewComment` (`codeReviewService.test.ts`). - :warning: Hygiene/compile and the test suites could not be executed in the authoring environment (no `node_modules`/build tooling). All changed files pass language-server diagnostics; please run the agentFeedback/codeReview unit tests in CI/locally before merging. title: sessions: rework New Chat UX in header, tabs and Conversations menu
body:
## What

Reworks the "New Chat" UX in the Agents (sessions) window across the session header, the chat tab strip, and the Conversations dropdown:

- **Header New Chat action** stays in the session header until the session has more than one **committed (non-draft)** chat — so it remains available even while an in-composer draft has surfaced the tab strip.
- **Chat tab strip** appears as soon as the session has more than one **open** chat (including in-composer drafts), and renders its own trailing **New Chat** action. It hides again (non-sticky) when chats are removed back down to just the main chat.
- **Conversations dropdown** is shown only once there is more than one committed chat. It opens with a **New Chat** entry, then lists each chat with a checkbox to show/hide it as a tab. Untitled draft chats are excluded from the toggle list.
- **Closing an untitled draft tab** deletes it without a confirmation prompt, via a new `IDeleteChatOptions.skipConfirmation` threaded through the delete-chat API and all providers (agent host, local chat sessions, copilot chat sessions).

## Why

Previously the tab strip was sticky and the single New Chat affordance/Conversations menu logic didn't cleanly reset when chats were deleted back to the main chat. This makes the header reset correctly and decouples the two signals: the tab strip tracks **open** chats (drafts included) while the header/Conversations switch tracks **committed** chats.

## Notes for reviewers

- New context key `SessionHasMultipleCommittedChatsContext` drives the header New Chat ↔ Conversations switch; the previous `SessionShowsChatTabsContext` (only ever written, never read after this change) was removed.
- `LAYOUT.md` updated to document the new non-sticky, open-vs-committed visibility behavior.
- This branch is stacked on `sandy081/maximize-editor-single-tab`; targeting `main` means the diff also contains that branch's editor commit until it merges.

title: chat: fix new-session picker no-op for extension chat sessions
body:
## now

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/572a8e6a-44eb-4888-835a-0cc5ba5de72b

## before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ffb296c-3caa-4ad6-82ff-02ce9b1f2c99






## Problem

Selecting an extension-contributed, non-delegating chat session in the new-session "harness" picker (e.g. **Codex** from the `openai.chatgpt` extension) does nothing — the selection doesn't change and no session opens.

The picker creates such a session by invoking `workbench.action.chat.openNewChatSessionExternal.<type>`. That command was only registered when `_registerMenuItems` happened to find an entry in `MenuId.AgentSessionsCreateSubMenu` **at the moment the contribution was enabled**. That snapshot races extension menu/command registration: for Codex the submenu is still empty at enable time, so the external command is never registered and never retried.

Clicking the entry then rejects with `command '...openai-codex' not found` (visible in the renderer log, not the extension output channel) and `_run` doesn't surface it, so the click silently no-ops.

```
[error] command 'workbench.action.chat.openNewChatSessionExternal.openai-codex' not found:
  Error: command 'workbench.action.chat.openNewChatSessionExternal.openai-codex' not found
```

## Fix

In `chatSessions.contribution.ts`:

- Register `openNewChatSessionExternal.<type>` **unconditionally** for non-delegating contributions, instead of only when the create submenu already has an entry.
- Resolve the underlying create-submenu command **lazily at execution time** (new `_resolveCreateSubMenuCommandId`), so it is unaffected by the ordering of extension menu/command registration.
- The action no-ops gracefully when no create command is contributed (instead of rejecting with "command not found").

The global Chat New menu mirroring behavior is preserved (the primary create action is still surfaced via the external command and is not duplicated into the menu).

## Result

Clicking **Codex** now reliably runs the extension's "New Codex Agent" command, opening a new Codex editor tab — the extension's intended behavior. Other harnesses (Local/Cloud/Copilot CLI, which are `canDelegate: true`) are unaffected.

## Testing

Verified manually in a dev build with the `openai.chatgpt` extension installed (`--enable-proposed-api openai.chatgpt`): Codex now opens its editor on click, and the `command ... not found` error no longer appears in the renderer log.

title: sessions: manage side pane and responsive sidebar in the layout controller
body:
## What

Consolidates side-pane and responsive-sidebar management into the session layout controller and fixes a sidebar-reveal bug after a window reload.

### Changes

- **Move the `Toggle Side Panel` action into the layout controller.** The action (and its "which parts were visible" memory) previously lived in `layoutActions.ts`. It now lives with the controller (`baseSessionLayoutController.ts`), registered when the contribution starts, so the side-pane visibility memory is owned by the component that manages the layout. `toggleSidePane()` is exposed for this.
- **Introduce `ISessionChangesService`** (`sessionChangesService.ts`) to own the `changes-multi-diff-source:` URI build/parse (identity), used alongside the upstream `IChangesViewService`. Updates `changesMultiDiffSourceResolver.ts`, `changesActions.ts`, and `changes.contribution.ts` to consume both services.
- **Fix the responsive sidebar reveal bug after reload (D7).** Previously the un-constrain auto-reveal was gated on an in-memory `_userClosedSidebar` flag that resets to `false` on reload, so closing the side pane after a reload wrongly revealed a sidebar the user had closed. The controller now tracks `_sidebarAutoHidden` and only auto-reveals a sidebar **it** auto-hid. After a reload the sidebar is already hidden, so the controller never "owns" that hidden state and leaves it closed.

## Why

Keeping the side-pane toggle and its memory inside the layout controller makes the responsive behavior coherent and lets the controller correctly distinguish controller-driven hides from user/reload state.

## Reviewer notes

- New regression test: `[D7] does not auto-show the sidebar the user closed before reloading`, plus new test-harness options `mainContainerWidth` and `initialPartVisibility`. Verified the test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- Validated: `typecheck-client` clean, 50 LayoutController tests passing, `valid-layers-check` clean, eslint clean, pre-commit hygiene passing.
- The spec doc `desktopSessionLayoutController.md` (D1-D9) was updated to describe the `_sidebarAutoHidden` behavior.

title: Handle XAA MCP account selection when provider account enumeration is empty
body:
Subsequent enterprise-managed MCP servers could fail with `No accounts available` even after successful XAA token exchange/redeem. The failure occurred when account enumeration returned empty while valid resource-scoped sessions already existed.

- **Root cause**
  - `AuthenticationMcpService.selectSession(...)` required `getAccounts(providerId)` to return accounts.
  - XAA/resource-scoped flows can legitimately have usable `availableSessions` even when provider-level account enumeration is empty.

- **Code change**
  - In `selectSession(...)`, account candidates now fall back to accounts derived from `availableSessions` (deduped by label) when `getAccounts(providerId)` is empty.
  - Existing behavior is unchanged when provider accounts are present.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added `authenticationMcpService.test.ts` with a focused case:
    - provider account list is empty
    - `availableSessions` has a valid enterprise account
    - selection succeeds instead of throwing `No accounts available`

```ts
const allAccounts = await this._authenticationService.getAccounts(providerId);
const seenSessionAccountLabels = new Set<string>();
const accountsFromAvailableSessions = availableSessions
	.map(session => session.account)
	.filter(account => !seenSessionAccountLabels.has(account.label) && seenSessionAccountLabels.add(account.label));
const accounts = allAccounts.length ? allAccounts : accountsFromAvailableSessions;
```

title: sessions: propose Draft Service for preserving unstarted session drafts
body:
Proposes a new Draft Service (`IAgentSessionsDraftService`) to preserve unsent message drafts (inputText and attachments) when the user navigates between unstarted or pending sessions in the Agents Window.

Currently, standard editor-level chat sessions successfully preserve drafts keyed by their session ID. However, the Agents Window homepage/composition view (`NewChatWidget` / `NewChatInputWidget`) uses a single global key (`sessions.draftState`) inside `IStorageService`. This leads to:
1. Message draft collisions between different unstarted sessions (e.g. sub-chats).
2. Immediate draft loss when switching away from the compose view (as the widget is disposed).

### Draft/Reference Implementation
This PR acts as a draft/reference implementation of the Draft Service pattern to demonstrate the fix. 
The goal of this PR is to:
- Propose the in-memory draft service pattern.
- Seek early validation from the team before completing a full, finalized implementation.
- Get steered in the correct direction if the team prefers a different architecture.

Closes #315996

title: Model picker: add settings to disable "Auto" grouping and expand "Other Models" by default
body:
### Summary

The Copilot model picker groups recently used models into a promoted "Auto" section at the top, and then **hides those same models from the remaining "Other Models" list**. On top of that, the "Other Models" section is collapsed by default, requiring an extra click every time to see the full list. Both behaviors make the picker harder to use, not easier — especially as the model list grows.

### Current behavior

1. Open the Copilot chat model picker.
2. Use any model (e.g. Claude Sonnet 4, GPT-5).
3. On the next open, that model appears in the promoted/Auto section at the top.
4. The model is **no longer visible in the full model list below** — it has been removed from its original position.
5. The "Other Models" section is **collapsed by default**, requiring a manual click to expand it every single time.

The result is that frequently used models exist only in the Auto section, sorted by recency with no stable ordering. Users who want to scan or compare models have to first expand a hidden section — and even then, recently used models won't appear there.

### Proposed settings

**1. Make the "Auto" promoted section optional**

Add a setting such as:
```
github.copilot.modelPicker.showRecentlyUsedGroup: true | false
```
When disabled, all models appear in a single flat list with a consistent ordering. Users who prefer the promoted section can keep it on; those who find it disorienting can turn it off.

**2. Allow the "Other Models" section to default to expanded**

Add a setting such as:
```
github.copilot.modelPicker.expandOtherModels: true | false
```
When enabled, the "Other Models" section opens expanded by default, avoiding the extra click on every picker open. This is independently useful even for users who keep the Auto grouping enabled.

### Why this matters

- The model list is already long and growing. Hiding models based on usage history makes it harder to find a specific model.
- Users who want to switch *away* from a recently used model may find it missing from the visible list entirely.
- Requiring a manual expand on every picker open adds unnecessary friction for anyone who regularly browses the full list.
- The deduplication logic powering this behavior also caused a separate bug where BYOK models with a `metadata.id` colliding with a built-in model's ID were hidden entirely from the picker (see #312908), suggesting the current design is worth reconsidering.

### Additional context

Related issues: #312908 (hidden BYOK models due to `metadata.id` collision in the same deduplication logic), #266950 (request to restore persistent model control), community discussion #187429 (disable Auto model selection).

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
In the June 2026 UX study, participants were familiar with the terms "session" and "chat" from other tools. However they consistently collapsed them into the same concept. 4/5 participants treated session and chat as one-to-one or identical. The product's multi-chat model requires users to understand that one session can hold many chats, but the shared vocabulary hides this gap.

"We call the chat… the session and chat is the same thing, right?" — Research participant

"It's just really like the conversation history, plus basically the actions that it's taken." — Research participant (describing "session" as if it were a single chat)

We know that the concepts are teachable, since participants learned the distinction when shown, but the current UI does not actively teach it.

Proposal
A design exploration to make the session/chat relationship visible through layout and defaults rather than relying on labels alone.

Directions to explore:

- Layout that spatially nests chats inside a session boundary (making the container relationship visible)
- Onboarding moment when a user creates their second chat in a session — explaining what just happened
- Visual language that distinguishes the session level (workspace, config, shared files) from the chat level (conversation, changes, agent)
- Default naming that reinforces the relationship (e.g., session named after the project, chats named after the task)

User evidence

- 4/5 participants collapsed session and chat into one concept
- 1 participant (P03) separated them unprompted but still mapped 1:1
- The distinction was learnable with moderator guidance but not self-evident from the UI
- Familiarity with the words across tools actively works against learning the new meaning

Design constraints

- Cannot rename "session" or "chat" without breaking cross-tool familiarity (P01 explicitly warned against terminology changes)
- Must work for first-time users who have never seen the Agents window
- Should not add friction for users who work with only one chat per session

title: Design the optimal experience for parallel work in the Agents window

labels.name: ux
labels.description: User experience issues

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
As we have seen from multiple studies, participants frequently run into difficulties managing parallel streams of work in the Agents window. Participants uniformly preferred serial work and struggled when pushed into parallelism. The tool did not make parallel work visible enough to manage easily or to entice participants to reduce their reluctance to adopt parallel workflows.

Key friction points:

- Cannot watch multiple streams simultaneously
- Lose track of which stream made which changes
- Cannot see what each agent is doing while it runs
- No summary of what each stream accomplished

Proposal
A design exploration to make parallel work manageable enough that the reluctance has a chance to soften.

Areas to explore:

- Side-by-side activity view — Show concurrent streams' progress simultaneously rather than requiring tab-switching
- Activity summaries — Replace wall-of-transcript with per-stream summaries of what happened and what changed
- Automatic worktree isolation — Create git worktrees per stream as an implementation detail, so parallel work cannot conflict at the file level
- Progress notifications — Show stream completion/error as toast or status-bar events so users don't need to watch constantly

User evidence

- 5/5 participants preferred serial work when left to their own devices
- When pushed into parallelism, all struggled with visibility and attribution
- Fear of streams conflicting was explicitly cited as a reason to avoid parallelism
- One participant proposed branch/worktree isolation as the solution

title: Make the changes that an agent has made immediately obvious

labels.name: ux
labels.description: User experience issues

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
During the June 2026 UX study participants universally wanted to see what the agent changed, quickly and directly. Getting to a clear, current diff was harder than it should have been. Participants frequently inspected the files view because they could see the color highlighting indicating where changes had been applied. But clicking on the files only showed the content of those files, not the diffs that had been applied. 

The desire to watch the work is strong, and the diff is part of the approval decision — not just a post-hoc review.

Proposal

- Make the diff one click away from any chat or agent activity — no hunting through transcript
- Provide more detail about proposed changes before approval when the agent requests permission to perform an action such as editing a sensitive file, so the user can make an informed allow/deny decision
- Ensure the diff is always current — if the agent makes additional changes, the view should update without requiring a manual refresh

User evidence

- 5/5 participants wanted to see what the agent changed
- Multiple participants hit bugs where changes did not display correctly
- Another wanted to see the diff before allowing an edit, not after
- The desire was universal across experience levels

Success criteria
[ ] Diff view reliably shows all new and modified files (no missing files)
[ ] Diff is reachable in one click from the active chat
[ ] Pending approval requests show a preview of the proposed change
[ ] Diff view updates in real-time as the agent makes additional changes

In the June 2026 UX study, participants found it difficult to keep track of what was happening across multiple sessions and within any chat that launched two or more sub-agents/sub-chats. When multiple agents share a transcript or run concurrently, their activity appears as an undifferentiated wall of text. Participants could not quickly determine which agent did what, or whether one stalled. When agents broke silently mid-task the failure was only discoverable by parsing the log manually.

Proposal
Give each active agent a distinct visual identity so that concurrent work is legible and attributable at a glance.

Design directions to explore:

- Per-session and/or per-agent colour coding or iconography in the chat transcript
- Visual separation (cards, borders, swimlanes) between sessions, agents and agent outputs
- Per-session and per agent status indicators showing: running, waiting, completed, errored
- Notifications when an agent stalls or errors, rather than requiring manual log inspection

- 2/5 participants had agents break silently mid-task with no visible indication
- Participants struggled to parse interleaved output from multiple agents
- One participant explicitly requested colour-coded separation by agent role
- Another wanted to "click in and see what they're doing" for each agent

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
From the recent June 2026 UX study, when multiple chats run within a session, participants expected to see what this chat changed, rather than what changed across the full workspace. This was the most consistently cited expectation (5/5 participants). However, the strength of this signal may partly reflect the study tasks, which deliberately pushed participants into parallel work. In practice, many developers work one stream at a time, and the pain of an unscoped changes view surfaces mainly when parallelism is in play.

"If I have five chats I don't know which chat made what changes… I would have to review 300 lines, and I don't know which chat did what." — Research participant

"I also can understand the technical limitations, so I could live with a diff just showing the whole [tree]… but maybe if the session view has a button to display the changes, I would expect it to be at the session level." — Research participant

Participants didn't necessarily ask for the changes view to change to show only changes per chat/session (many equated chat and session), they requested a way to see the changes that had been made by the agent in a chat/session.

It would be worth exploring ways in which we can show and summarise changes made by the agent in the visible chat or session and exploring whether changes made by other means, such as an agent working inside VS Code, or the developer making manual edits need to be summarised in the same way.

For example:

- could the existing Changes view panel be filtered/toggled by stream?
- Inline in the chat conversation at the end of each agent turn (summary of what just changed)?
- Both — a lightweight inline summary plus a detailed view on demand?

Other things to consider during the exploration are that in this study, participants were pushed into parallelism. We know from other studies that this not the default behaviour. Would developers who work serially (the observed default) encounter this pain naturally?

If not, should this be optimised for the parallel case specifically, rather than changing the default single-stream experience?
What's the right fidelity for an inline summary?

Full diff inline?
File-list with change counts (e.g., "Modified: api/tags.ts (+12 −3), Created: tests/tags.test.ts")?
Expandable summary that links to the full diff?

Design directions worth prototyping

- Inline turn summary: At the end of each agent turn, show a collapsible "Changes made" card listing files modified/created/deleted, with a "View diff" link to the detailed view
- Scoped Changes view toggle: Add a filter to the existing Changes panel to scope by chat/stream
- Per-chat changes tab: Each chat gets its own changes section (separate from the workspace-wide panel)

User evidence

- 5/5 participants expected changes to be attributable to a chat/session
- Experienced participants understood git constraints and proposed workable seams
- One participant proposed a side-panel (whole project) + session-control (scoped view) split
- Another reached for separate branches/worktrees as file-level isolation

title: Update input needed session animations with pulsing background
body:
This pull request introduces a visual indicator for session rows that require input by adding a pulsing yellow background animation. The animation is suppressed when the row is selected or when the user has enabled reduced motion preferences. These changes have been applied to both the sessions list and agent sessions viewer components.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0225aebb-c54d-45ac-b684-b9767975852c


Visual enhancements for "Input needed" sessions:

* Added a pulsing yellow background animation for session rows that need input in `sessionsList.css` and `agentsessionsviewer.css`. The effect is suppressed when the row is selected to avoid overpainting the selection highlight. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd9669576e99ab30bc76563f9128ed7eae19675968e6c1e7ba8f9119d4c858baR17-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51debdf07c55b26d7182061708f3f76c081701584eb8f6187352f0b463f25c64R29-R40)
* Implemented `@keyframes` animations (`session-needs-input-accent-pulse` and `agent-session-needs-input-accent-pulse`) for the pulsing effect, using a mix of the warning foreground color and transparency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd9669576e99ab30bc76563f9128ed7eae19675968e6c1e7ba8f9119d4c858baR494-R503) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51debdf07c55b26d7182061708f3f76c081701584eb8f6187352f0b463f25c64R447-R456)
* Provided accessibility support by disabling the animation and using a static background color when the user prefers reduced motion. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd9669576e99ab30bc76563f9128ed7eae19675968e6c1e7ba8f9119d4c858baR17-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51debdf07c55b26d7182061708f3f76c081701584eb8f6187352f0b463f25c64R29-R40)

VS Code ships the Claude and Codex agents but not their native binaries — those download on demand from the CDN (70–95 MB compressed) the first time a session of that type starts, then cache. On a cold cache the first turn blocks for several seconds with **no feedback** (it looks hung). This surfaces a progress indicator in the Agents window instead.

## What you see

A toast in the Agents window — "Downloading Claude…" / "Downloading Codex…" — filling 0→100% (determinate when the CDN sends `Content-Length`, indeterminate otherwise), clearing on completion.

## How it works

The download runs in the **agent host** (utility process locally, or the remote server over WSL/SSH); the UI is in the **renderer**. Progress crosses the agent-host protocol via the new `root/downloadProgress` notification:

1. `agentSdkDownloader._fetch` counts received bytes vs `Content-Length`, throttles, and fires `onDidDownloadProgress`.
2. The local/remote bridges map it onto the generic AHP frame (`kind: 'agent-sdk'`, `resourceId`, `phase`) through the state manager — the same fan-out path as session notifications, so it reaches both local (IPC) and remote (WebSocket) clients.
3. The Agents window renders it as an `IProgressService` toast keyed by `downloadId`.

Also gates Codex's eager prewarm-on-create so it no longer triggers a cold download with no user action — the download now happens on first message.

## Depends on

Vendors the protocol types from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#263, which defines `root/downloadProgress`. **That PR should merge first** — it's the source of truth for the wire contract; the vendored copy here (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/`) mirrors it.

title: sessions: drag & drop to reorder workspaces and groups in the sessions list
body:
## What

Adds drag & drop reordering of **workspace section headers** and **user-group headers** in the Agents window sessions list. Dragging a group/workspace header over another shows an insertion line above/below it to position it there.

### Behavior
- **By Workspace:** user groups and workspace sections share **one freely-intermixable, user-managed order** below Pinned. Groups default above workspaces; workspaces default alphabetical ("Unknown" last) until dragged. Dragging a workspace **promotes** it so it stays visible (escapes the "+N more workspaces" capping).
- **By Date:** user groups form a **contiguous, user-ordered block** directly below Pinned and never mix into the fixed date sections (Today/Yesterday/...). Only group headers are draggable in this mode.
- **Invariants:** Pinned is always first and Done always last; neither (nor the date sections, nor "show more" rows) is draggable or a valid drop target.
- **Groups are now fully user-managed:** their order no longer derives from member-session recency and is **shared across both grouping modes** (it also drives the "Add to Group" / "Move to Group" menu order).

## How
- New `ISessionSectionOrderService` (`services/sessions/browser/sessionSectionOrderService.ts`) owns the manual top-level order as an explicit list of identities (`group:<id>` / `workspace:<label>`) plus a promoted-workspaces set. Persisted locally (profile storage), not synced. Includes pure, unit-tested helpers (`resolveSectionOrder`, `spliceSectionOrder`, `mergeSectionOrder`) and stale-identity garbage collection.
- `sessionsList.ts`: generalized the DnD from group-only to any reorderable header (`reorderSection` + `IDraggedHeader`), made workspace headers draggable, and rewrote both render branches to use the resolved order (capturing a display-order snapshot for the drop math and applying workspace promotion to the capping).
- Removed the obsolete `sortKeyOverride` / `setGroupSortKey` / `groupSortKey` member-recency mechanism from `sessionGroupsService.ts`.
- Updated `SESSIONS_LIST.md` and added/adjusted unit tests.

## Notes for reviewers
- Design replaces an earlier numeric "midpoint sort key" approach with an explicit ordered-id list, which avoids mixed numeric-key-domain fragility and makes promotion independent of ordering.
- **Not validated locally** (no `npm install` in this environment): `npm run typecheck-client`, the sessions unit tests, and hygiene/lint were **not** run. IDE language-service diagnostics were clean across all touched files. Relying on CI for validation.
- Follow-up (not in this PR): keyboard-accessible reordering — kept parity with the existing DnD-only reordering for sessions; recommend adding "Move Up/Down" for sessions and headers together in a separate change.

## 2. Choosing Your Destination

France offers very different experiences depending on the region. Pick based on your vibe:

- **Paris** 🗼 — Iconic city break: museums, cafés, architecture. (~4h by train)
- **Lyon** 🍽️ — Gastronomy capital, charming old town. (~4h by train)

- **Zurich HB → Paris Gare de Lyon**: ~4h direct on **TGV Lyria** (high-speed).

- Book early via **SBB**, **TGV Lyria**, or **Rail Europe** for the best fares.

- Direct flights from **Zurich (ZRH)** to Paris, Lyon, Nice, Marseille (~1–1.5h).
- Best for the Riviera or far-south destinations.
- Factor in airport transfer + security time (~3h total door-to-door).

### 🚗 By Car
- Zurich → Paris: ~6.5h (650 km).

- Flexible for the countryside; remember the **Swiss motorway vignette** and French **tolls (péages)**.

## 4. Sample Itinerary (Paris, 5 Days)

### Day 1 — Travel & Arrival
- Morning TGV Lyria from Zurich HB.

### Day 2 — Classic Paris
- **Eiffel Tower** & Champ de Mars.
- **Louvre** or **Musée d'Orsay**.
- Sunset from **Trocadéro** or a Seine river cruise.

### Day 3 — Neighborhoods
- **Montmartre** & Sacré-Cœur.
- **Le Marais** for shopping and cafés.
- Evening cabaret or a quiet wine bar.

### Day 4 — Day Trip
- **Versailles** palace & gardens, or
- **Giverny** (Monet's gardens, seasonal).

### Day 5 — Departure
- Morning at a café / last-minute shopping.
- Afternoon TGV back to Zurich.

- [ ] Travel insurance details

## 7. Practical Tips

- **Money**: Switzerland uses CHF, France uses EUR — withdraw/exchange before crossing.
- **Trains**: Validate reservations; TGV requires a seat reservation.
- **Language**: A few French phrases (*bonjour, merci, s'il vous plaît*) go a long way.
- **Tipping**: Service is included in France; round up for good service.
- **Connectivity**: An EU/Swiss-inclusive eSIM avoids roaming surprises.
- **Safety**: Watch for pickpockets in busy tourist areas and on transit.
- **Opening hours**: Many shops/museums close on Mondays or Sundays — check ahead.

Fixes #244138
## Problem
When an extension is globally disabled but enabled for a workspace, the Disable button dropdown incorrectly shows both Disable and Disable (Workspace) items.
## Root Cause
Both DisableGloballyAction and DisableForWorkspaceAction never set their hidden flag, so ButtonWithDropDownExtensionAction always included both items in the dropdown regardless of state.
## Changes
- DisableGloballyAction.update(): only shows when extension is EnabledGlobally (was: EnabledGlobally || EnabledWorkspace), sets hidden when not applicable
- DisableForWorkspaceAction.update(): only shows when extension is EnabledWorkspace, fixes a misplaced parenthesis bug that put getWorkbenchState() inside the .some() callback, sets hidden when not applicable
